# `ptfkit.rudiyanto2021`

```cpp
import ptfkit.rudiyanto2021;
```

**Exported namespace:** `ptfkit::rudiyanto2021`

Rudiyanto et al. (2021), neuroFX hydraulic parameters from saturation to dryness.

## Source

Rudiyanto, Minasny, B., Chaney, N. W., Maggi, F., Goh Eng Giap, S., Shah, R. M., Fiantis, D., & Setiawan, B. I. (2021). Pedotransfer functions for estimating soil hydraulic properties from saturation to dryness. Geoderma, 403, 115194.

[DOI: 10.1016/j.geoderma.2021.115194](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.geoderma.2021.115194)

## Scope

**Dataset:** Selected UNSODA laboratory drying data, excluding Andisols: 215 soils, 2224 retention observations and 3646 conductivity observations. Bulk density is available for 210 soils with 2142 retention and 3580 conductivity observations. Eleven USDA textural classes are represented.

[PTF catalog page](../../../ptf-catalog/sources/rudiyanto2021.md)

## `NeuroFXTextureClass`

The eleven soil textural classes in Table 1; no sandy clay class is supplied.

## `Rudiyanto2021Parameters`

```cpp
struct Rudiyanto2021Parameters {
    double theta_s;
    double alpha;
    double n;
    double m;
    double k_sat;
    double tortuosity;
};
```

| Field | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `theta_s` | Saturated volumetric water content of the FXW retention model. (cm³ cm⁻³) |
| `alpha` | Inverse pressure-scale parameter in the FXW relative saturation function. (cm⁻¹) |
| `n` | FXW retention shape parameter n, fitted independently of m. (-) |
| `m` | FXW retention shape parameter m, fitted independently of n. (-) |
| `k_sat` | Saturated hydraulic conductivity of the FXW conductivity model. (cm d^-1) |
| `tortuosity` | Pore tortuosity and connectivity parameter of the FXW conductivity model. (-) |

## Functions

### `calc_ptf_rudiyanto2021_sscbd` {#function-calc_ptf_rudiyanto2021_sscbd}

Estimate six FXW hydraulic parameters from texture fractions and bulk density.

```cpp
[[nodiscard]]
inline Rudiyanto2021Parameters calc_ptf_rudiyanto2021_sscbd(double sand, double silt, double clay, double bulk_density)
```

#### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `sand` | Sand mass fraction for particles from 50 to 2000 micrometers. (kg/kg) |
| `silt` | Silt mass fraction for particles from 2 to 50 micrometers. (kg/kg) |
| `clay` | Clay mass fraction for particles smaller than 2 micrometers. (kg/kg) |
| `bulk_density` | Soil dry bulk density used by the SSCBD neural network. (g/cm^3) |

#### Returns

A `Rudiyanto2021Parameters` value.

!!! note

    Texture inputs are mass fractions from 0 to 1 and must sum to one.

!!! note

    Return the ensemble mean in each network's output scale, then backtransform alpha, n and saturated conductivity as in evaluate_nnet_grid.R. These are not arithmetic means of the individually backtransformed hydraulic parameters.

!!! note

    The ensemble contains all 50 fitted realizations; uncertainty outputs are not returned.

!!! warning

    The paper describes texture percentages; the supplied R program and its grid instead use fractions. Do not pass percentages to this interface or rescale the supplied weights.

!!! warning

    Training uses UNSODA drying data; no generalization beyond that data is established.

### `calc_ptf_rudiyanto2021_texture` {#function-calc_ptf_rudiyanto2021_texture}

Return six median FXW hydraulic parameters for a soil textural class.

```cpp
[[nodiscard]]
inline Rudiyanto2021Parameters calc_ptf_rudiyanto2021_texture(NeuroFXTextureClass soil_texture)
```

#### Parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `soil_texture` | Soil textural class used to select the Table 1 median FXW parameters. |

#### Returns

A `Rudiyanto2021Parameters` value.

!!! note

    Table 1 medians, rather than means, define the class PTF in sections 2.3.1 and 3.3.3. Bulk density is not returned as a hydraulic parameter.

!!! note

    Parameters n and m are independent FXW parameters; do not impose the van Genuchten restriction m = 1 - 1/n.

!!! warning

    Some classes have few observations; sandy clay is not represented.

!!! warning

    Independent-soil validation of the class PTF is identified as future work in section 3.3.3.
